sa: किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम।
tr: kiṃ tadbrahma kimadhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama
en: What is that Brahman? What is the Self within? What is action, Purushottama? What is called the realm of beings, and what the realm of the gods?
speaker: Arjuna said

en: Who is the lord of sacrifice here in this body, and how, Madhusudana? And how are you to be known at the hour of death by those who are self-controlled?
The imperishable is the supreme Brahman; its own nature is called the Self within; the creative force that brings beings into existence is called action.
speaker: Krishna said

en: The realm of beings is the perishable; the realm of the gods is the cosmic Person; and I myself, here in the body, am the lord of sacrifice, best of the embodied.

sa: यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥
tr: yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ
en: Whoever leaves the body at the time of death remembering me alone comes to my being; of this there is no doubt.

sa: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्।
tr: yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram
en: Whatever state of being one remembers when leaving the body at the end, to that one goes, son of Kunti, having always been absorbed in it.
So remember me at all times, and fight. With mind and intellect offered to me, you will surely come to me.
With a mind disciplined by practice, not wandering elsewhere, constantly meditating, one reaches the supreme divine Person, Partha.
One should meditate on the Seer, the ancient, the ruler, smaller than the atom, the sustainer of all, of unthinkable form, radiant like the sun, beyond all darkness;
at the time of departure, with an unmoving mind, joined in devotion and by the strength of yoga, drawing the life-breath fully between the brows, one reaches that supreme divine Person.
What the knowers of the Veda call the imperishable, what ascetics free from passion enter, what people keep celibacy to reach: that state I will describe to you briefly.

sa: सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च।
tr: sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca
en: Closing all the gates of the body, holding the mind in the heart, drawing the life-breath into the head, established in the concentration of yoga,

sa: यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
tr: yaḥ prayāti tyajandehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim
en: uttering Om, the one-syllable Brahman, and remembering me, whoever departs leaving the body reaches the highest goal.

sa: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः।
tr: ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ
en: For one who remembers me constantly, every day, with mind never turned elsewhere, I am easy to reach, Partha, for that ever-disciplined yogi.
Having come to me, great souls who have reached the highest perfection do not return to rebirth, that impermanent home of sorrow.

sa: मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥
tr: māmupetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate
en: All worlds, up to the realm of Brahma, return again, Arjuna; but having come to me, son of Kunti, there is no rebirth.
Those who know that a day of Brahma lasts a thousand ages, and his night a thousand ages, truly know day and night.
At the coming of that day, all manifest things emerge from the unmanifest; at the coming of night they dissolve into that same unmanifest.

sa: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते।
tr: bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate
en: This same multitude of beings, coming into being again and again, dissolves helplessly at the coming of night, Partha, and emerges again at the coming of day.

sa: यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥
tr: yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
en: But beyond that unmanifest there is another, eternal unmanifest being, which does not perish when all beings perish.

sa: यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
tr: yaṃ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama
en: That unmanifest is called the imperishable; they call it the highest goal. Those who reach it do not return. That is my supreme abode.

sa: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया।
tr: puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyastvananyayā
en: That supreme Person, Partha, in whom all beings dwell and by whom all this is pervaded, is reached by undivided devotion.

sa: प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥
tr: prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha
en: Now I will tell you, best of the Bharatas, the times at which yogis depart never to return, and at which they return.

sa: तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
tr: tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ
en: Fire, light, day, the bright fortnight, the six months of the sun's northern course: departing then, knowers of Brahman go to Brahman.
Smoke, night, the dark fortnight, the six months of the sun's southern course: departing then, the yogi reaches the light of the moon and returns.

sa: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते।
tr: śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate
en: These two paths, the bright and the dark, are thought to be eternal for the world. By one, one goes and does not return; by the other, one returns again.

sa: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन।
tr: naite sṛtī pārtha jānanyogī muhyati kaścana
en: Knowing these two paths, Partha, no yogi is ever deluded. So at all times, Arjuna, be steadfast in yoga.
Whatever merit is said to come from the Vedas, from sacrifices, austerities and gifts, the yogi who knows this goes beyond it all and reaches the supreme, primal abode.
